blocks.text: Sifat otni tasvirlaydi (a **quick** lunch — tezkor tushlik), ravish (adverb) esa **fe'lni** — harakat qanday bajarilishini: eat **quickly** — tez ovqatlanmoq. O'zbek tilida ko'pincha ikkalasi uchun bitta so'z ishlatiladi: **tez** mashina — **tez** haydamoq, **yaxshi** odam — **yaxshi** gapirmoq. Ba'zan «... bilan» yoki `-cha` qo'shiladi: **ehtiyotkorlik bilan**, **do'stona**. Ingliz tilida esa ravish odatda alohida shaklga ega: sifat + `-ly`. Shuning uchun o'zbeklar ko'pincha «He drives careful» deb xato qiladi.

Qaysi birini tanlash uchun so'z **nimani** tasvirlayotganiga qarang. Ot yoki olmoshni (kim? nima? qanday?) — **sifat**: Aziz is a **careful** driver. Fe'lni (qanday qilib? qay tarzda?) — **ravish**: Aziz drives **carefully**. Ikki gapning ma'nosi deyarli bir xil, faqat birida «haydovchi» (ot), ikkinchisida «haydaydi» (fe'l) tasvirlanyapti. be, look, feel kabi fe'llardan keyin sifat kelishini unutmang (85-dars): He **is** careful, He **looks** careful.

Ko'pchilik sifatga shunchaki `-ly` qo'shiladi: slow → slow**ly**, polite → polite**ly**. `-l` bilan tugagan sifatda `l` saqlanadi, shuning uchun ikkita `l` chiqadi: careful → careful**ly**, real → real**ly**, usual → usual**ly**. `-y` → `-ily`: easy → eas**ily**, happy → happ**ily**, angry → angr**ily**. `-le` bilan tugaganlarda `e` tushib qoladi: terrible → terrib**ly**, possible → possib**ly**, gentle → gent**ly**.

**good** — sifat, uning ravishi — **well** («goodly» degan so'z yo'q): Your English is **good** → You speak English **well**. **well** yana bir ma'noda **sifat** bo'lib keladi — «sog', sog'lom»: How are you? — I'm very **well**, thanks. I don't feel **well** — Mazam yo'q. Solishtiring: You look **good** (Ko'rinishingiz zo'r, chiroyli kiyinibsiz) va You look **well** (Sog'lom ko'rinasiz).

items.text: I'm sorry, but I don't feel **well** today.

blocks.text: Ba'zi so'zlar sifat ham, ravish ham bo'ladi va shakli o'zgarmaydi: **hard**, **fast**, **late**, **early**. a **fast** car — drive **fast** («fastly» degan so'z yo'q). Ehtiyot bo'ling: **hardly** va **lately** ham bor, lekin ular boshqa ma'noli so'zlar: **hardly** — «deyarli ... emas» (I **hardly** know him — Uni deyarli tanimayman), **lately** — «so'nggi paytlarda».

Ravish odatda fe'ldan keyin keladi, to'ldiruvchi bo'lsa — to'ldiruvchidan keyin: She speaks English **well** («She speaks well English» emas). Fe'l bilan to'ldiruvchi o'rtasiga ravish qo'yilmaydi. **suddenly** kabi ravishlar gap boshida ham kelishi mumkin. Ravish sifat oldida uning darajasini ham ko'rsatadi: **really** cold (juda sovuq), **terribly** sorry (juda afsusdaman). So'z tartibi batafsil — 93–94-darslarda.

O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: «He drives very careful» → He drives very **carefully**; «You play chess very good» → You play chess very **well**; «She speaks well English» → She speaks English **well**; «I work hardly» (= deyarli ishlamayman!) → I work **hard**; «He runs fastly» → He runs **fast**; «You look tiredly» → You look **tired** (look dan keyin sifat — 85-dars).
Tekshirish usuli: so'zga «qanday odam / qanday narsa?» deb savol bera olsangiz — sifat (a **careful** driver); «qanday qilib bajaradi?» deb savol bera olsangiz — ravish (drives **carefully**).

rows: shakli o'zgarmaydi; hardly, lately — boshqa ma'no

examples.title: **-ly** adverbs: **slowly**, **quietly**, **suddenly**
examples.description: Ravish harakat **qanday** bajarilishini aytadi va ko'pincha sifat + `-ly` dan yasaladi: slow → **slowly**, quiet → **quietly**. O'zbekchada ko'pincha shu so'zning o'zi yoki «... bilan»: **sekin** gapirmoq.

sentences.text: Please speak **slowly** — my English isn't very good.
sentences.translation: Iltimos, **sekin** gapiring — inglizcham unchalik yaxshi emas.

sentences.text: The baby is sleeping, so close the door **quietly**.
**Suddenly** the lights went out.
Bekzod answered all the questions **correctly**.
Why are you talking so **loudly**? Everybody can hear you.
sentences.translation: Nega bunchalik **baland ovozda** gapiryapsan? Hamma eshityapti.

sentences.text: Madina smiled **warmly** at her guests.
My little sister writes very **neatly**.
Over the hills the sun was shining **brightly**.
Tom opened the letter and read it **quickly**.
The plane landed **safely**, and all the passengers clapped.
sentences.translation: Samolyot **eson-omon** qo'ndi, barcha yo'lovchilar qarsak chalishdi.

examples.title: Adjective or adverb? **careful** / **carefully**
examples.description: Sifat otni (qanday odam? qanday narsa?) tasvirlaydi, ravish — fe'lni (qanday qilib?): Aziz is a **careful** driver — he drives **carefully**. O'zbekchada ikkalasi ko'pincha bir xil so'z: **tez** mashina — **tez** haydamoq.

sentences.text: Aziz is a **careful** driver.
He always drives **carefully**, even on empty roads.
sentences.translation: U doim, hatto bo'm-bo'sh yo'lda ham **ehtiyotkorlik bilan** haydaydi.

sentences.text: Sarah has got a very **quiet** voice.
She speaks so **quietly** that I can't hear her.
That was a **bad** mistake.
I slept **badly** because of the noise outside.
There was a **sudden** noise, and the dog jumped up.
The weather changed **suddenly**, and it started to rain.
Dilnoza is very **polite**, and she always answers the phone **politely**.
sentences.translation: Dilnoza juda **odobli**, telefonga ham doim **xushmuomalalik bilan** javob beradi.

sentences.text: The instructions were **clear**, so we built the table **quickly**.
sentences.translation: Ko'rsatmalar **aniq** edi, shuning uchun stolni **tez** yig'ib oldik.

sentences.text: You can **easily** find our house — it's next to the mosque.
The children were playing **happily** in the garden.
I'm **terribly** sorry — I forgot your birthday.
The waiter looked at us **angrily** and walked away.
sentences.translation: Ofitsiant bizga **jahl bilan** qaradi-yu, ketib qoldi.

sentences.text: Tom **really** wants to visit Uzbekistan next year.
sentences.translation: Tom kelasi yili O'zbekistonga borishni **juda** xohlaydi.

sentences.text: Explain it **simply** — the children are only seven.
sentences.translation: **Sodda** qilib tushuntiring — bolalar endi yetti yoshda.

sentences.text: Hold the baby **gently** — she's only two weeks old.
sentences.translation: Chaqaloqni **ehtiyotlab** ushlang — u endi ikki haftalik.

sentences.text: The students listened **carefully** to the guide in Bukhara.
Aziz and his brothers ate their dinner **hungrily**.
sentences.translation: Aziz va akalari kechki ovqatni **ishtaha bilan** yeyishdi.

sentences.text: Our plane was late, but **luckily** we didn't miss the train.

examples.title: **good** and **well**
examples.description: **good** — sifat (a **good** cook), **well** — ravish (cooks **well**). «Goodly» degan so'z yo'q. **well** sog'liq haqida sifat bo'lib ham keladi: he isn't **well** — mazasi yo'q.

sentences.text: Your English is very **good**.
You speak English **well** — where did you learn it?
sentences.translation: Ingliz tilida **yaxshi** gapirar ekansiz — qayerda o'rgangansiz?

sentences.text: Is Madina a **good** singer? — Yes, she sings really **well**.
sentences.translation: Madina **yaxshi** xonandami? — Ha, u juda **yaxshi** kuylaydi.

sentences.text: How did you sleep? — Not very **well**, I'm afraid.
Bekzod can't come to work today — he isn't **well**.
sentences.translation: Bekzod bugun ishga kela olmaydi — **mazasi yo'q**.

sentences.text: The concert was **good**, and the band played **well**.
Grandma doesn't see very **well** without her glasses.
Did the interview go **well**? — Yes, I think so.
sentences.translation: Suhbat **yaxshi** o'tdimi? — Ha, shunday deb o'ylayman.

sentences.text: James is a **good** footballer, but he doesn't play **well** in the rain.
sentences.translation: Jeyms **yaxshi** futbolchi, lekin yomg'irda **yaxshi** o'ynay olmaydi.

sentences.text: This cake tastes **good** — you bake really **well**!
sentences.translation: Bu tortning **ta'mi zo'r** — juda **yaxshi** pishirar ekansiz!

examples.title: **hard**, **fast**, **late**, **early**
examples.description: Bu so'zlar sifat ham, ravish ham bo'ladi va `-ly` olmaydi: a **fast** train — drive **fast**. **hardly** («deyarli ... emas») va **lately** («so'nggi paytlarda») — boshqa ma'noli so'zlar.

sentences.text: Aziz works very **hard** — he often stays at the office until nine.
sentences.translation: Aziz **tinim bilmay** ishlaydi — ko'pincha ofisda soat to'qqizgacha qoladi.

sentences.text: This is a **hard** question. Can you help me?
The train to Samarkand is very **fast**.
Don't drive so **fast** — the road is wet.
Sorry I'm **late** — the traffic was terrible.
On Fridays Emma works **late** and gets home at ten.
sentences.translation: Juma kunlari Emma **kechgacha** ishlaydi va uyga soat o'nda keladi.

sentences.text: We need to catch an **early** flight tomorrow.
My father gets up **early** every day, even on Sundays.
sentences.translation: Otam har kuni, hatto yakshanba kunlari ham **erta** turadi.

sentences.text: I **hardly** know my new neighbours — we only say hello.
Have you seen James **lately**? — No, he's been very busy.
sentences.translation: **So'nggi paytlarda** Jeymsni ko'rdingizmi? — Yo'q, u juda band edi.

examples.title: How ...? — **Very carefully**: questions and answers
examples.description: «Qanday qilib?» (How ...?) yoki «Tez yozadimi?» kabi savollarga ko'pincha ravish bilan javob beriladi: How does he drive? — **Carefully**.

sentences.text: How does your brother drive? — Very **carefully**, like an old man.
sentences.translation: Akang qanday haydaydi? — Xuddi choldek, juda **ehtiyotkorlik bilan**.

sentences.text: Does Bekzod type fast? — Yes, he types very **quickly**.
sentences.translation: Bekzod tez yozadimi? — Ha, u juda **tez** yozadi.

sentences.text: Did you sleep **well** last night? — Yes, **perfectly**.
How did Sarah speak at the meeting? — **Clearly** and **confidently**.
sentences.translation: Sara yig'ilishda qanday gapirdi? — **Aniq** va **ishonch bilan**.

sentences.text: Can your daughter swim? — Yes, and she swims really **well**.
sentences.translation: Qizingiz suzishni biladimi? — Ha, juda **yaxshi** suzadi.

sentences.text: Was the guide friendly? — Yes, she answered all our questions **patiently**.
sentences.translation: Gid samimiy edimi? — Ha, barcha savollarimizga **sabr bilan** javob berdi.

sentences.text: Why are you walking so **slowly**? — My feet hurt.
How did the children do in the exam? — Very **well** — they all passed.
sentences.translation: Bolalar imtihonda qanday natija ko'rsatdi? — Juda **yaxshi** — hammasi o'tdi.

sentences.text: Does it rain **heavily** in Manchester? — Yes, very often in autumn.
sentences.translation: Manchesterda **kuchli** yomg'ir yog'adimi? — Ha, kuzda tez-tez.

sentences.text: Is Dilnoza's French good? — Yes, she speaks it **fluently**.
sentences.translation: Dilnozaning fransuz tili yaxshimi? — Ha, u **ravon** gapiradi.

examples.title: **looked sad** or **looked sadly** at?
examples.description: be, look, feel, smell, taste, sound dan keyin — sifat (egani tasvirlaydi): She **looked sad**. Oddiy harakat fe'lidan keyin — ravish: She **looked sadly** at the photo (qanday qaradi?).

sentences.text: Madina **looked sad** when her friend left.
Madina **looked sadly** at the empty chair.
The soup **tastes good** — you cooked it really **well**.
You **sound happy** today! — Yes, I've got a new job.
sentences.translation: Bugun ovozingiz **xursand eshitilyapti**! — Ha, yangi ishga kirdim.

sentences.text: The children were laughing **happily** in the next room.
Tom **felt nervous**, so he spoke **quickly** and forgot half of his speech.
sentences.translation: Tom **hayajonlandi**, shuning uchun **tez** gapirib, nutqining yarmini unutdi.

sentences.text: Is the coffee **hot**? — Yes, drink it **slowly**.
The flowers **smell sweet**, and the bees are working **busily** around them.
Aziz is usually **quiet**, but yesterday he argued **angrily** with his boss.
sentences.translation: Aziz odatda **kamgap**, lekin kecha boshlig'i bilan **jahl bilan** tortishdi.

sentences.text: Your plan **sounds good**, but we need to think about it **carefully**.
sentences.translation: Rejangiz **yaxshi** ekan, lekin uni **puxta** o'ylab ko'rishimiz kerak.

examples.title: Mixed: adjective or adverb?
examples.description: Aralash mustahkamlash: har bir gapda so'z nimani tasvirlayotganiga qarang — otni (sifat) yoki fe'lni (ravish).

sentences.text: Sarah isn't a **bad** driver, but she parks **badly**.
sentences.translation: Sara **yomon** haydovchi emas, lekin mashinani **yomon** qo'yadi.

sentences.text: The bus was **late** again, so I walked to work **quickly**.
sentences.translation: Avtobus yana **kechikdi**, shuning uchun ishga **tez** yurib bordim.

sentences.text: My grandfather speaks **slowly**, but his mind is very **quick**.
sentences.translation: Bobom **sekin** gapiradi, lekin fikri juda **tez** ishlaydi.

sentences.text: Our new teacher explains grammar very **clearly**.
sentences.translation: Yangi o'qituvchimiz grammatikani juda **tushunarli** qilib tushuntiradi.

sentences.text: Dilnoza didn't study **hard**, but she passed the exam **easily**.
The rain stopped **suddenly**, and the sky became **clear**.
You look **tired** — did you sleep **well**?
James played the piano **beautifully** at his sister's wedding.
In London people walk **fast** and rarely stop to talk.
sentences.translation: Londonda odamlar **tez** yurishadi va gaplashish uchun kam to'xtashadi.

sentences.text: This bag is **cheap**, but it's **really well** made.
